chunks: Al-Ḥusayn ibn Muḥammad, from Muʿallā ibn Muḥammad, from Al-Washshāʾ, from Ḥammād ibn ʿUthmān, from Zurārah, from Abī Jaʿfar (عليه السلام), who said:
The Messenger of Allah (صلى الله عليه وآله) prescribed the blood-money for the eye and the blood-money for the life, and he prohibited nabīdh and every intoxicant.
So a man said to him: "Did the Messenger of Allah (صلى الله عليه وآله) prescribe that without anything having come regarding it?"
He said: "Yes, so that He may know who obeys the Messenger from those who disobey him."

key_terms.النَّبِيذَ: nabīdh, a fermented drink mentioned here as prohibited
key_terms.دِيَةَ النَّفْسِ: the prescribed blood-money for a human life
key_terms.دِيَةَ الْعَيْنِ: the prescribed financial compensation for injury causing loss of an eye
key_terms.يَعْصِيهِ: disobeys him by refusing or violating his command
key_terms.يُطِيعُ الرَّسُولَ: obeys the Messenger in what he commands and legislates

ai.seo_question: Can the Messenger of Allah (صلى الله عليه وآله) establish legal rulings whose obedience is independently required?
ai.summary: This hadith states that the Messenger of Allah (صلى الله عليه وآله) legislated specific rulings, including compensation for bodily injury and the prohibition of intoxicants. It also affirms that obedience to the Messenger is itself a divine test distinguishing those who obey him from those who disobey him.
